en kæbe.explanation: "En kæbe" means "a jaw". To say a jaw is broken, use "at brække" (to break): "Han har brækket kæben" (He has broken his jaw).

en kæde.explanation: "En kæde" means "a chain". When you talk about shops owned by one company, it also means a group of shops: "en kæde af butikker" (a chain of stores).

en kælder.explanation: "En kælder" means "a basement". To say where you keep things, use "i kælderen" (in the basement): "Vi opbevarer cyklerne i kælderen" (We keep the bikes in the basement).

en kæledyrsforsikring.explanation: "En kæledyrsforsikring" means "a pet insurance policy". It is built from "et kæledyr" (a pet), the joining "s" and "en forsikring" (an insurance policy). To say you took out a policy, use "at tegne" (to take out): "Vi har tegnet en kæledyrsforsikring til hunden" (We have taken out pet insurance for the dog).

en kæmpe.explanation: "En kæmpe" means "a giant". When you put "kæmpe" before another word, it means "huge": "en kæmpe fejl" (a huge mistake).

en kæreste.explanation: "En kæreste" means "a partner (romantic)". It is the same word for a man and a woman. To ask someone about their love life, say: "Har du en kæreste?" (Do you have a boyfriend or girlfriend?)

en kø.explanation: "En kø" means "a queue". To say you wait in line, use "at stå i kø" (to stand in a queue), with no "en": "Vi står i kø til biografen" (We are standing in line for the cinema). When you talk about cars, it also means a traffic jam: "Der er kø på motorvejen" (There is a traffic jam on the highway).

en københavner.explanation: "En københavner" means "a Copenhagener". It is built from "København" (Copenhagen). Other cities have a similar word, such as "en aarhusianer" (a person from Aarhus): "Min ven er aarhusianer" (My friend is from Aarhus).

en købmand.explanation: "En købmand" means "a grocer / shopkeeper". It is built from "at købe" (to buy) and "en mand" (a man). To say you shop at the local grocer's, say: "Jeg handler hos købmanden" (I shop at the grocer's).

en kødbolle.explanation: "En kødbolle" means "a meatball". It is built from "kød" (meat) and "en bolle" (a ball). In the Danish dish "boller i karry" (meatballs in curry), the meatballs are called just "boller": "Vi spiser boller i karry til middag" (We eat meatballs in curry for dinner).

en kødspiser.explanation: "En kødspiser" means "a meat eater". The opposite is "en vegetar" (a vegetarian): "Han er vegetar" (He is a vegetarian).

en køjeseng.explanation: "En køjeseng" means "a bunk bed". It is built from "en køje" (a bunk) and "en seng" (a bed). To say which bunk you sleep in, say: "Jeg sover i den øverste køje" (I sleep in the top bunk).

en køkkenchef.explanation: "En køkkenchef" means "a head chef". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en chef" (a boss). To say what someone does for a living, say: "Hun er køkkenchef på en restaurant" (She is head chef at a restaurant).

en køkkenhave.explanation: "En køkkenhave" means "a vegetable garden", literally "a kitchen garden". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en have" (a garden). A garden for flowers only is "en prydhave" (an ornamental garden): "Der er blomster og buske i prydhaven" (There are flowers and bushes in the ornamental garden).

en køkkenrulle.explanation: "En køkkenrulle" means "a roll of paper towels". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en rulle" (a roll). To ask someone to pass it, say: "Kan du række mig køkkenrullen?" (Can you hand me the paper towels?)

en køkkenvægt.explanation: "En køkkenvægt" means "a kitchen scale". It is built from "køkken" (kitchen) and "en vægt" (a scale). The word "vægt" also means "weight": "Jeg vil gerne tabe vægt" (I want to lose weight).

en kørelærer.explanation: "En kørelærer" means "a driving instructor". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en lærer" (a teacher). The verb "at køre" is also used for going by vehicle: "Jeg kører med bussen" (I go by bus).

en køreplan.explanation: "En køreplan" means "a timetable". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en plan" (a plan). To find out when a bus leaves, use "at tjekke" (to check): "Jeg tjekker køreplanen for bussen" (I check the timetable for the bus).

en køreprøve.explanation: "En køreprøve" means "a driving test". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en prøve" (a test). To say you sit the test, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager køreprøven i næste uge" (I am taking the driving test next week).

en køreskole.explanation: "En køreskole" means "a driving school". It is built from "at køre" (to drive) and "en skole" (a school). To say you have a lesson, use "en køretime" (a driving lesson): "Jeg har en køretime i morgen" (I have a driving lesson tomorrow).

en kørestol.explanation: "En kørestol" means "a wheelchair". To say someone uses a wheelchair, use "sidde i kørestol" (sit in a wheelchair), with no "en": "Han sidder i kørestol" (He uses a wheelchair).

en kørsel.explanation: "En kørsel" means "a drive / trip". On a road sign, it names the act of driving: "Kørsel forbudt" (No driving).

et kaffebord.explanation: "Et kaffebord" means "a coffee-and-cake gathering". In Denmark, it is held after a christening, a confirmation or a funeral. The table in a living room is a different thing, "et sofabord" (a living-room table): "Kopperne står på sofabordet" (The cups are on the living-room table).

et kaffefilter.explanation: "Et kaffefilter" means "a coffee filter". It is built from "kaffe" (coffee) and "et filter" (a filter). The plural is "kaffefiltre" (coffee filters), not "kaffefiltere", because the "e" before "r" drops out.

et kalenderlys.explanation: "Et kalenderlys" means "an Advent calendar candle". In Denmark, it is a candle marked with the numbers 1 to 24, which you burn down one number each day in December. It is built from "en kalender" (a calendar) and "et lys" (a candle).
